title: Lutathera for the treatment of recurrent Meningioma (LUMEN-1)
official: EORTC 2334-BTG: [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE for recurrent MENingioma (LUMEN-1): a randomized phase II study
summary: Main objective: This randomized phase II trial aims to examine whether [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE demonstrates sufficient antitumor activity in patients with recurrent meningioma (as measured by progression free survival (PFS) to support the potential clinical use of [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in patients with recurrent meningioma with limited therapeutic options, and to provide supportive evidence for future regulatory submissions.
conditions: Recurrent Meningioma without local treatment options (Surgery or Radiotherapy)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adult patient ≥ 18 years of age
2. At least one prior surgery and one line of external beam radiotherapy for meningioma, if technically feasible
3. Adequate liver, renal and haematological function within four weeks prior to enrolment
4. Participants must have the potassium, magnesium, total calcium electrolyte values within normal limits or corrected to be within normal limits with supplements prior to first dose of study medication.
5. Patients who are receiving corticosteroid treatment with dexamethasone, must be treated with a dose of ≤4 mg/day (or other corticosteroids equivalent dose) for a minimum of 7 days prior to the initiation of study treatment.
6. Patients of childbearing / reproductive potential should use adequate birth control measures during the study treatment period and for at least 7 months after the last dose of treatment. A highly effective method of birth control is defined as a method which results in a low failure rate (i.e., less than 1% per year) when used consistently and correctly.
7. Female subjects who are breast feeding should discontinue nursing prior to the first dose of study treatment and until 7 months after the last study treatment.
8. Before patient 's enrolment, written informed consent must be given according to ICH/GCP, and national/local regulations.
9. Histologically confirmed diagnosis of meningioma (all grades, 1-3 per WHO CNS5, are eligible)
10. WHO performance status 0-2
11. Measurable disease (at least 10 x 10 mm contrast enhancing lesion) on cranial MRI no more than two weeks prior to enrolment
12. Radiologically documented progression of any existing tumour (growth > 25% increase in the product of perpendicular diameters of any enhancing lesion in the last two years) or appearance of new lesions (including intra- and extracranial manifestations), as per RANO meningioma criteria.
13. Somatostatin receptor (SSTR)-positive confirmed by PET imaging with scan performed within four weeks before randomization (baseline SSTR-PET is considered as positive when meningioma uptake intensity exceeds a SUVmax of 2.3). In the case of multiple lesions, SUVmax exceeding 2.3 will be required at least for a target lesion.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Local therapy (surgery and / or radiotherapy) indicated per local investigator. Note: in case of patients with multiple meningioma lesions, in whom resection and / or radiotherapy of individual lesions is indicated, patients may be included after local therapy (with a 4-week gap between surgery / end of radiotherapy and start of treatment), if at least one remaining lesion fulfils the inclusion criteria.
2. Any prior systemic treatment regardless of the timing.
3. Life expectancy is less than nine weeks.
4. Prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment has the potential to interfere with the safety or efficacy assessment of the study treatment.
5. Contraindication to MRI, CT or PET
6. Unstable cardiac conditions (congestive heart failure, angina pectoris, myocardial infarction within one year before enrolment, uncontrolled hypertension, clinically significant arrhythmias)
7. Psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical conditions could potentially hamper compliance with the study protocol and follow-up schedule.
8. Known hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any excipients.
9. Medical history of leukaemia or myelodysplastic syndrome.
